processing: Orthodox Ceylon black tea made in the usual grades, such as OP and FBOPF1.
harvest_season: Little is published on a particular season for this estate; Sri Lankan tea is generally picked through the year.
appearance_dry: Dark orthodox leaf, long and wiry in OP and smaller in the FBOP grades.
appearance_liquor: Bright reddish amber; a bright liquoring FBOPF1 is what auction reports praise.
taste_profile: Little is recorded in detail; expect a medium-bodied, bright Ceylon black tea, with OP lighter and FBOP grades stronger.

brewing.notes: Brewed Western style. A splash of milk suits the smaller grades; OP is better plain.

vintage_note: Mostly sold through the Colombo auction by grade and without a vintage, then packed by retailers as current-season tea. As with other Ceylon single-estate teas, buy recent lots and drink them within a year or two.
description:
Pettiagalla is a Balangoda estate in the Sabaragamuwa hills. It is mostly known in the trade, through the Colombo auction, rather than to people buying a packet.

It makes orthodox black tea in standard grades. An FBOPF1 has set an estate record at auction, in the Uva Medium category, even though the estate sits outside Uva proper.

Brew it as a sturdy daily tea. Water just off the boil and three minutes is enough, and the smaller grades will take milk.

In the West it shows up mainly as an occasional single-estate OP from specialist shops. Treat any story about the name as decoration, and look at the grade and how recent the lot is.
history:
The Tamil politician S. J. V. Chelvanayakam was at one point part of a syndicate that bought a controlling stake in the estate.

It is managed by Balangoda Plantations. At the weekly auction of 14 March 2022 an FBOPF1 reached an all-time estate record of Rs. 1,180 per kilo in the Uva Medium category.
